draft.title: Darwin, Wallace and the theory of evolution
card: Charles Darwin and Alfred Russel Wallace each proposed natural selection from their own observations of living things in different places.
Their ideas were made public together in 1858. Darwin later published a detailed book on the idea in 1859.
Darwin and Wallace did not know how traits are passed on. Later work in genetics showed that genes carry traits and that changes in genes cause variation.
This new evidence strengthened the theory and refined it, because it explained how variation arises and is inherited.
draft.remember: Two people proposed natural selection from observation, and genetics later explained how traits are inherited.

a.q: Which statement about the origin of the theory of natural selection is correct?
opts: Darwin and Wallace each proposed it from observations
Only Darwin proposed it, and Wallace opposed it
Genetics experiments in the 1900s first proposed it
Wallace proposed it after reading Darwin's 1859 book
a.why: Both men reached natural selection from their own observations. Saying only Darwin proposed it leaves out Wallace, who worked it out independently.
a.clue: Think about how many people reached the idea.

b.q: What did later work in genetics add to the theory of evolution?
opts: An explanation of how variation arises and is inherited
Proof that natural selection never happens
The first idea that species change over time
A way to make organisms identical to one another
b.why: Genetics showed that genes carry traits and that gene changes cause variation, which Darwin and Wallace could not explain. It strengthened the theory rather than replacing it. Cloning is a different idea and is not part of this.
b.clue: Darwin and Wallace did not know how traits were passed on.

a.best: Darwin and Wallace each proposed it from observations

b.best: An explanation of how variation arises and is inherited

problems.detail: The right option is clearly the longest and repeats the card's wording ('how variation arises and is inherited'), so a student could pick it without knowing the idea.

proposal.title: Darwin, Wallace and the theory of evolution
card: Charles Darwin and Alfred Russel Wallace each proposed natural selection from their own observations of living things in different places.
Their ideas were made public together in 1858. Darwin later published a detailed book on the idea in 1859.
Darwin and Wallace did not know how traits are passed on. Later work in genetics showed that genes carry traits from parents to offspring, and that changes in genes cause variation.
This new evidence strengthened the theory and refined it, because it explained where variation comes from and how it is inherited.
proposal.remember: Two people proposed natural selection from observation, and genetics later explained how traits are inherited.

a.q: Which statement about the origin of the theory of natural selection is correct?
opts: Darwin and Wallace each proposed it from observations
Only Darwin proposed it, and Wallace opposed it
Genetics experiments in the 1900s first proposed it
Wallace proposed it after reading Darwin's 1859 book
a.why: Both men reached natural selection from their own observations. Saying only Darwin proposed it leaves out Wallace, who worked it out independently.
a.clue: Think about how many people reached the idea.

b.q: Darwin saw that birds of one species differed in beak size, but could not explain where the differences came from. What did later work show?
opts: Changes in genes passed from parents to their young
Birds reshaping their beaks by use during their lives
Food on the island directly reshaping each bird's beak
Wallace's notes on birds from other islands
b.why: Genetics showed that variation comes from changes in genes, and genes carry traits from parents to offspring. A beak changed by use during a bird's life is not carried in its genes, so it does not explain inherited differences. Wallace's observations, like Darwin's, did not explain how traits are passed on.
b.clue: Where are traits carried, so they can pass to the next generation?

a.best: Darwin and Wallace each proposed it from observations

b.best: Changes in genes passed from parents to their young
